original_question: Characterize the numerical semigroups that can be written as quotients S / p = {x in N | px in S} of numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 3 by a positive integer, and determine whether every numerical semigroup arises in this way.
target_in_paper: Section 3, unnumbered open problem after the definition of the quotient S/p: determine which numerical semigroups occur as quotients of embedding-dimension-three numerical semigroups by a positive integer, and whether any numerical semigroup fails to be of this form. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Section 3 quotient operation S/p = {x in N | px in S}, the restriction to source numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 3, and the paper's second issue: whether every numerical semigroup might arise this way, equivalently whether any counterexample exists. It also stays in the right part of the paper rather than drifting to unrelated later topics. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: The quantified object should be a given target numerical semigroup T; the question is whether T can be recognized as T = S/p for some numerical semigroup S and some positive integer p, not to classify source semigroups S in isolation. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The existential quantifiers should be explicit: there should exist a numerical semigroup S and an integer p >= 1 such that T = S/p = {x in N : px in S}. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Embedding dimension should be defined: e(S) is the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S, and the source semigroup must satisfy e(S) = 3. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To match the paper more closely, the task should be framed as finding a criterion or procedure that distinguishes such quotients from arbitrary numerical semigroups, not only as an abstract global characterization. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: numerical semigroups are subsets of N = {0,1,2,...} that contain 0, are closed under addition, and have finite complement in N. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

No additional hypotheses are part of this problem: there is no ambient ring or field, no homogeneity or degree condition, no nilpotency assumption, and no asymptotic phrase such as for all sufficiently large m; the problem is purely semigroup-theoretic. This is a clarification of scope from the paper's setup. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: Given a numerical semigroup T ⊆ N = {0,1,2,...}, determine whether there exist a numerical semigroup S and a positive integer p such that e(S) = 3, where e(S) denotes the cardinality of the minimal system of generators of S, and T = S/p := {x in N : px in S}; more specifically, find a criterion or procedure that distinguishes numerical semigroups of this form from those that are not, and decide whether any numerical semigroup fails to arise in this way. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: The draft maps directly to Section 3. There the paper defines the quotient S/p, recalls that the embedding-dimension-two case is understood, and then says that the next step is to study quotients of embedding-dimension-three numerical semigroups. The paper's two concrete open ends are exactly the ones your draft is reaching for: no procedure is known to distinguish such quotients from the rest, and no example is known of a numerical semigroup that is not of this form. I did not replace this with the later, broader page-18 question about characterizing whole families of semigroups under fixed-denominator quotients, because that is a neighboring but more general problem. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
